Reports by Jacqui Smiter

Nina Mills was next away, clocking 19:02 to bring the team in 9th, and a now constantly improving Jacqui Smiter enjoyed herself on the final leg, picking off two of the opposition with her 17:56 effort.

She was also a member of the Southern Women's 3 x 800m gold medal winning team in 1987, along with Jacqui Smiter and Jackie Stone. Jacinta has been Track Captain since 1986 when she saw the team finish 7th in their first season in the Southern Women's League Division 2, narrowly missing promotion direct to Division 1.
These were Alex Barber, Angela Patten, Julia Cockram and Jacqui Smiter, and our best on record has been broken in three out of the six league matches.

Angela Patten and Gail Richardson covered the throws between them leaving Jacqui Smiter to fill in all the gaps. The two "J's", Georgina and Angela finally managed to compete in both relays with about 10-15 minutes rest.
Sue Drummie was 8th with 2.50, Julia Cockram 9th with 2.30 and Jacqui Smiter was unable to clear her opening height - just the sort of problem Mike Edwards sometimes has!

It was good to have Jacqui Smiter back in the team after months of problems with shin splints and we welcomed two new under 15s to bolster our younger section - thrower Michelle Stock and sprinter Melissa Bentt.
